question.leadin: This man was shot and killed by a Union soldier after the barn where he was hiding was set on fire.
question.text: Name this stage actor who shouted "Sic semper tyrannis" as he assassinated Abraham Lincoln.
question.clue: Samuel Mudd created a splint for this man's broken leg.

swap.leadin: The repulsion of Pickett's Charge at Cemetery Ridge secured victory in this battle for Union forces.
swap.text: Identify this pivotal battle of the Civil War in Pennsylvania, where Joshua Chamberlain led Union forces in a downhill bayonet charge at Little Round Top.
swap.clue: The "high-water mark" of this battle's losing side was achieved by Pickett's Charge.

question.text: The Liberator was published by Isaac Knapp and this man, who infamously burned a copy of the Constitution in 1854, calling it an "Agreement with Hell" for its support of slavery.
question.clue: Arthur and Lewis Tappan splintered from one society started by this man.

swap.leadin: Victoria Woodhull named this man her running mate on the Equal Rights Party presidential ticket in 1872.
swap.text: Name this abolitionist and former slave who described his experiences in brilliant orations and the autobiography Narrative of the Life.
swap.clue: He was taught the alphabet by Hugh Auld, his master's wife, and later founded the newspaper The North Star.

question.leadin: The highest-ranking Confederate general, Albert Sidney Johnston, was killed during this battle.
question.text: Name this battle, which began after P.G.T. Beauregard launched a surprise attack on Pittsburg Landing.
question.clue: General Albert Sidney Johnston was killed during this battle, becoming the highest ranking Civil War officer to die on the field.

swap.text: The issue of slavery in the new territories prompted the signing of this agreement, which saw California admitted as a free state and the establishment of popular sovereignty for deciding whether or not a territory would allow slavery.
swap.clue: The Seventh of March Speech byDaniel Webster supported this legislation, and one of its components upheld so-called "Bloodhound Laws."

question.leadin: After the Civil War, this man served as the governor of Rhode Island.
question.text: Name this Union general who was famous for his namesake facial hair.
question.clue: This first president of the NRA led the failed Mud March in an attempt to capture Richmond.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about boats used during the Civil War.
swap.text: The Confederates made this first ironclad, which sat largely underwater, from a captured frigate. It totally wrecked everything until it fought the Union ironclad Monitor inconclusively at Hampton Roads.
swap.clue: The Battle of Hampton Roads took place between the USS Monitor and this confederate ship, also the name of the state where Hampton Roads is located.

question.leadin: T-Bonus 2. Identify these cases from United States legal history.
question.text: Roger Taney heard this case as a circuit judge despite being Chief Justice of the Supreme Court at the time. It concerned a Maryland officer involved in the ejection of Union troops from Baltimore, and declared that Lincoln's denial of habeas corpus was unconstitutional.
question.clue: The defendant's trouble began with his burning of a bridge in Parkton, for which he lost his position in the Baltimore County Guards and was detained by General George Cadwalader in Fort McHenry, prompting Chief Justice Taney to argue for his release.

swap.leadin: Name these other Civil War battles.
swap.text: By forcing General Pemberton's forces to surrender on July 4th, 1863, after a six-week siege of this city, Grant cut the Confederacy in two.
swap.clue: It's not Atlanta, but the first bottling of Coca-Cola took place here in 1891.

question.leadin: Juanita Brooks is best known for her books about this event, which her grandfather Dudley Leavitt may have participated in.
question.text: Name this event. The only person tried for participating in it, John D. Lee, said "I have been sacrificed in a cowardly, dastardly manner" before being executed by firing squad.
question.clue: During this event, a militia dressed up as Paiute ] Indians killed members of the Baker-Fancher wagon train.

swap.text: The KKK's first Grand Wizard was this man, who as a cavalry officer during the Civil War, during which he became famous for his audacious charges and habit of executing black Union prisoners.
swap.clue: He disgustedly asked "What does he fight battles for?" after disagreeing with Braxton Bragg after the Battle of Chickamauga.

question.leadin: Name these Civil War era songs with further impact on US politics.
question.text: This song, whose title alludes to Sherman's March to the Sea, was played to honor many veterans at political nominations. A performance of it by a Northern band at the 1924 DNC pissed off KKK members among the Southern delegation.

swap.leadin: Even though he was on trial for murder, Vice President Aaron Burr still presided over the impeachment of a politician with this last name.
swap.text: Give this surname of the first Supreme Court justice to be impeached. A different politician with this last name presided over Texas v. White as Chief Justice in the aftermath of the American Civil War.
swap.clue: A man with this last name added "In God We Trust" on coinage and succeeded Roger Taney's post after Taney's death.

question.leadin: This commander First Bull Run saw his command given to Braxton Bragg after he withdrew from Corinth without a major battle and took unauthorized medical leave.
question.text: Name this Acadian confederate commander who was in charge of Charleston's defenses the night Fort Sumter was attacked.
question.clue: This general who commanded men fighting Robert Anderson in an 1861 battle. His forces at a later battle won against the Union when he was commanding the Confederate troops with Joseph Johnston at Manassas.

swap.text: From his committee chairmanship, Stevens was instrumental in passing this constitutional amendment, which banned slavery in the United States.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the career of an American military leader.
question.text: At San Diego, Kearny joined his army with the forces of this naval commander, now the namesake of a city in central California. They later had a quarrel over who should be governor of the territory, which resulted in Kearney's arrest of John C. Fremont.
question.clue: This commodore built the Peacemaker gun that blew up in the Princeton disaster, but he was cleared of blame. He's also remembered for replacing John Sloat as the commander of the U.S. Pacific Squadron and using his flagship, the USS Congress, to do battle in Alta California.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about acoustic shadows, or areas in which the propagation of sound waves is blocked.
swap.text: Similarly, Joseph Johnston arrived late to this battle, the culmination of the Peninsula campaign, because of an acoustic shadow. Johnston's injury at this battle led Robert E. Lee to take over as commander.
swap.answerHtml: Battle of Seven Pines [or Battle of Fair Oaks Station]
swap.clue: Howard fought in this two day Civil War battle during the Peninsular Campaign. Fought six miles east of Richmond, it saw the Confederates commanded by Joseph Johnston, who was wounded on the first day.

question.text: This New York governor made a militia out of the Albany sheriff's posse to put down the first uprising and set up a commission to find redress for farmers' grievances. Later in life, he lost the 1860 Republican presidential nomination to Lincoln and was nearly assassinated by Lewis Paine.
question.clue: He helped resolve the Trent Affair as Secretary of State.

swap.leadin: This man murdered Francis Scott Key's son, Phillip Barton Key, but was acquitted due to temporary insanity.
swap.text: Name this man who also served as a Union General at Gettysburg, and controversially moved his troops to Peach Orchard.
swap.clue: A star team of lawyers that included Edwin Stanton and James T. Brady helped acquit this person using the first ever plea of temporary insanity.
